Rarity.rationale: Matches SelfFormingClay.cs:19. Obtainable: Uncommon in the transcribed grab bag (relic_pools.py:171, 'RELIC.SELF_FORMING_CLAY'). Rule 7: relic_pools.py is not hashed here.

AfterDamageReceived.maps_to: on_damage_received (self_forming_clay.py:29-38) for the LATCH, plus on_player_turn_started (self_forming_clay.py:40-46) for the PAYOUT -- the sim replaces C#'s SelfFormingClayPower with a relic-local `_pending_block` counter, so one C# hook plus one whole power map onto two sim methods
AfterDamageReceived.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and N3 per binding rule 4. The latch is faithful (owner check, unblocked-damage > 0, +3 per HP-loss event, killing-blow guard inherited from cmds.py:121) but the RE-ARCHITECTURE of the payout is where the divergences are: C# banks the block in a PowerModel that dies with the combat and pays out at AfterBlockCleared, and the sim banks it on the relic instance -- which lives on RunState.relics -- and pays out at on_player_turn_started, ~12 steps later in the turn. That makes state cross the combat boundary (G1, LIVE) and moves the payout past listeners that damage the player in between (G2, LIVE), and it deletes a visible player power (N3).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): `_pending_block` survives the combat, so a fight that ends before the player's next turn hands free Block to the NEXT combat
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# has no relic-side counter at all. SelfFormingClay.cs:29 applies a SelfFormingClayPower to the owner and SelfFormingClayPower.cs:19-25 pays it out at AfterBlockCleared and then removes itself, so the pending block is a POWER -- and powers do not survive a combat. self_forming_clay.py:27 puts the counter on the relic instead, and relic instances live on RunState.relics and are re-attached to every new CombatState, so anything unspent latches for the rest of the run. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed with ported content only -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b14.py clay-carry): playing Hemokinesis (cards/hemokinesis.py:37, a ported Ironclad Uncommon whose 2 HP self-loss goes through DamageCmd) as the killing blow leaves combat 1 over with `_pending_block = 3`, and the next CombatState opens turn 1 with `block = 3` where a fresh instance -- and C# -- gives 0. Both sides ported and nothing further is needed: the relic is Uncommon in the grab bag and every run has more than one combat. Other reachable shapes: any unblocked damage taken during the player's own final turn (Bloodletting, Offering, Brand, Blood Wall all route HP loss through DamageCmd), or a Thorns enemy retaliating on the killing blow (monsters/hive/spiny_toad.py:45 and monsters/underdocks/toadpole.py:75 both apply ThornsPower). CORRECTION TO A SWEEP -- this unit is a FALSE CLEAR: py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset files self_forming_clay in the bucket labelled 'RESET AT TURN START, BEFORE ANY READER (art_of_war shape -- genuinely safe)'. The reset is not before the reader: self_forming_clay.py:41-46 pays the block out on line 43 and only zeroes the field on line 46, so it is a consume-then-clear. The sweep's bucket test looks at WHICH METHOD writes a field, never at whether the write precedes the read inside it. That is a seventh sweep-A defect and the third of the false-clear kind; it is reported in .superpowers/sdd/relic-batch-14-lessons.md with the executed evidence. Rule 7: cards/hemokinesis.py, monsters/hive/spiny_toad.py, monsters/underdocks/toadpole.py, run.py, combat.py and relic_probes.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE): the payout moved from AfterBlockCleared (turn_structure step ~11) to on_player_turn_started (step 23), so damage taken IN BETWEEN is paid out the same turn instead of the next
guards.issue: MECHANISM: SelfFormingClayPower.AfterBlockCleared (SelfFormingClayPower.cs:19-25) fires in the block-clear pass, before the energy reset, before ModifyHandDraw and before the whole AfterPlayerTurnStart / AfterSideTurnStart region (audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json steps 11 through 23). self_forming_clay.py:40 uses on_player_turn_started, the LAST turn-start slot. Any effect that damages the player between those two points is therefore banked and paid in the SAME turn by the sim, and banked now / paid next turn by C#. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b14.py clay-slot): Royal Poison damages its owner from AfterPlayerTurnStart (RoyalPoison.cs:18, step 22, ported at relics/royal_poison.py), which is inside the window. With relics registered [royal_poison, self_forming_clay] the sim opens turn 1 with block = 3; with [self_forming_clay, royal_poison] it opens with block = 0 and `_pending_block = 3`. C# gives turn-1 block 0 in both cases, because the Clay power is applied after the block clear has already run. Both sides ported and obtainable: Royal Poison is a ported relic and Self-Forming Clay is Uncommon in the grab bag. The sentinel trace in the same probe shows the payout is invisible at every earlier slot (on_block_cleared / on_energy_reset / on_player_turn_start / modify_hand_draw all read block 0). Note this is NOT merely seam guard G12's flat-pass problem: the two relics are in DIFFERENT C# passes AND the sim's Clay is in the wrong slot entirely, so separating the passes alone would not fix it. Rule 7: turn_structure.json, relics/royal_poison.py, RoyalPoison.cs and SelfFormingClayPower.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: the sim has no SelfFormingClayPower at all, so the pending Block is not a visible, stackable, removable power on the player
guards.issue: MECHANISM: `grep -rn SelfFormingClay sts2_rl/powers.py` returns nothing -- the sim models the effect as a private int on the relic. In C# it is a real PowerModel with `Type => Buff` and `StackType => Counter` (SelfFormingClayPower.cs:13-15), which means it is enumerated by CombatState.IterateHookListeners, is subject to PowerCmd's whole pipeline on application (Hook.ModifyPowerAmountGiven, Artifact, the sign-aware typing), can be read by anything that inspects the player's powers, and can be removed or doubled. The sim's counter can be none of those things. DORMANT, with the concrete unported/absent things named: (a) doubling -- relic/unsettling_lamp only doubles Debuffs, so a Buff-typed Counter power is out of its reach, and no ported effect doubles a player Buff; (b) removal -- no ported enemy power or card removes a player Buff by type; (c) reading -- no ported listener enumerates the player's Buff powers looking for a block-granting one. Porting any buff-stripping enemy move, any 'double your Buffs' effect, or any effect that reads player Buff amounts makes it live. Filed as a gap rather than a deliberate-divergence because the observable is a power that exists on one side and not the other, which a replay comparison of the player's power list would see immediately. Rule 7: powers.py, cmds.py and audit/records/relic/unsettling_lamp.json are not hashed here.

guards.what: N1: `result.UnblockedDamage > 0` (SelfFormingClay.cs:27) vs the sim's `amount > 0`, where amount is DamageCmd's post-modifier hp_lost (cmds.py:122)
guards.rationale: Checked because UnblockedDamage could plausibly mean pre-HP-loss-modifier damage, which would make Tungsten Rod's -1 a divergence. It does not: Creature.LoseHpInternal builds the DamageResult with `UnblockedDamage = currentHp - CurrentHp` (Creature.cs:453), i.e. HP actually lost, and CreatureCmd.Damage runs both Hook.ModifyHpLost phases BEFORE LoseHpInternal (CreatureCmd.cs:266-272). The sim's pipeline is the same order (cmds.py:84-93) and passes the same post-modifier `hp_lost` to on_damage_received. EXECUTED (relic_probes_b14.py clay-carry): 5 damage fully absorbed by 10 Block banks 0; a following 12 into the remaining 5 Block banks exactly 3 (one application, not one per point). Rule 7: Creature.cs, CreatureCmd.cs and cmds.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N2: the killing-blow guard (PROMPT.md class 2) and `CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress` (SelfFormingClay.cs:27)
guards.rationale: C# skips the victim's AfterDamageReceived when the hit kills it (CreatureCmd.cs:392's `!WasTargetKilled || !IsDead`), and the sim honours it at the dispatcher: cmds.py:121 wraps the call in `if not target.is_dead`. So a lethal hit on the player banks nothing on either side -- which matters only if a death is later prevented, and Fairy in a Bottle's revive path goes through after_preventing_death (cmds.py:111-113), not on_damage_received, on both sides. IsInProgress is structurally satisfied: on_damage_received is a combat hook, and out-of-combat HP loss goes through RunState.lose_hp / modify_run_hp_loss instead (relics/base.py:222-228). Rule 7: cmds.py, relics/base.py and CreatureCmd.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N4: `target == base.Owner.Creature` (SelfFormingClay.cs:27) vs `target is self.player` (self_forming_clay.py:37) -- identity, not side
guards.rationale: Both compare identity against the owning player's creature, so unlike relic/unsettling_lamp G3's side-vs-identity split there is no divergence to record: C# also uses `==` on the creature here rather than `Side ==`. Recorded because the two shapes are easy to conflate and the Lamp's record verdicts the other one a gap. A player-side minion would be excluded by both.

guards.what: N5: the BLOCK amount -- DynamicVar("BlockNextTurn", 3m).BaseValue (SelfFormingClay.cs:21, :29) vs BLOCK = 3 (self_forming_clay.py:23), and the block's props
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in either file, so 3 is the pinned non-ascension value, and Counter stacking means repeated applications sum -- which `self._pending_block += self.BLOCK` reproduces. The payout props match too: SelfFormingClayPower.cs:23 grants `CreatureCmd.GainBlock(Owner, Amount, ValueProp.Unpowered, null)` and self_forming_clay.py:44 passes props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED, so Dexterity and Frail do not scale it on either side. Rule 7: SelfFormingClayPower.cs and cmds.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N6: ExtraHoverTips (SelfFormingClay.cs:23), the _blockNextTurnKey const, and the PlayerChoiceContext parameter
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / UpdateDisplay / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Title / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd / CardPreviewStyle are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, the localized name, and animation timing.
